h1:
Isan Food in Sisaket
Som Tam, Larb, Koi and Grilled Chicken Locals Actually Eat
intro: Sisaket is a town where eating Isan-style is second nature, because people here have som tam, larb and koi at pretty much every meal. The genuinely good places usually aren't fancy at all, they're the spots locals keep coming back to. We picked these from local reviews and tell you the area, the rough prices, and what to order at each one.
chips: 🍗 Grilled chicken for a few baht

blocks.html: Sisaket's Isan food carries a southern-Isan accent: spicy and savory from fermented fish (pla ra), but with a fragrant, Khmer-influenced touch on some dishes. The places locals actually go to are mostly roadside som tam stalls or small larb shops that have been around for years, and prices are still very reasonable, around 30–60 THB a plate for som tam and just a few tens of baht for half a grilled chicken. We've gathered the spots that come up most often in reviews, with a straight take on what each one does best.

blocks.text: Ranking Sisaket's Isan restaurants that locals actually eat at

blocks.html: This ranking is ordered by how often each place comes up in reviews and how popular it is with locals, not a claim that the lower spots are less tasty. Each one has its own strengths, so pick by the dishes you want and the area that's convenient for you. Prices are rough per-plate estimates and may shift with the time of day and ingredients.

items.name: Som Tam Si Phao Sisaket
items.blurb: A well-known som tam spot in town that leans on Sisaket's "four peoples" (Lao, Suay, Khmer, Yer) as its hook. There's a wide range of som tam, bold and properly Isan in flavor, in a relaxed, unfussy setting. Locals drop in for both lunch and dinner.
items.meta: Nong Khrok, Mueang district · open 08:00–19:00 daily

items.name: Tam Kratoey Sisaket
items.blurb: A som tam shop locals talk up for the cook's touch and seriously punchy flavors. The pla ra crab som tam is deeply savory, and there's larb and rice dishes to order alongside. The vibe is friendly neighborhood-stall, good for a quick lunch.
items.meta: Sisaket town center · lunch to dinner
items.price: Som tam 40–60 THB · single plates 40–50 THB

items.name: Larb Sisaket
items.blurb: An old larb shop on the main road beside Da Ling Inn, next to the Krasaeng noodle place. The draw is cheap prices and quick service: grilled chicken, grilled offal, tom saep, larb and koi, the lot. Good for a relaxed, easy-on-the-wallet meal with friends.
items.meta: On the main road beside Da Ling Inn · in town

items.name: Larb Saeng Siri
items.blurb: A larb spot for spice lovers with a full menu: pork larb, giant snakehead larb, pla ra crab som tam, plus unusual local dishes like om nuea and seua rian for people who genuinely want to try local food. It's over in the Warin Chamrap direction toward Ubon, worth a stop if you're driving past.
items.meta: Ubon–Sisaket Rd, Huai Khayung, Warin Chamrap · 08:00–18:30

items.name: Mae Noi Grilled Chicken
items.blurb: A regular grilled-chicken spot around Kanthararom, near the train station, where locals often grab takeaway. The chicken is fragrant with marinade and crisp-skinned, perfect with som tam and hot sticky rice, at a wallet-friendly price. Good to bag up and eat on the go.
items.meta: Kanthararom district, near the train station
items.price: Grilled chicken from 60–120 THB/bird · som tam 40 THB

items.name: Grilled Pork Rice Sisaket (Mueang Tai area)
items.blurb: Despite the name being grilled-pork rice, the standout is the grilled pork neck eaten with Isan-style som tam and larb. The pork is tender and fragrant, great with a punchy jaew dip. It's open from late morning to evening, ideal if you want both grilled pork and som tam in one place.
items.price: Grilled pork 50–90 THB · som tam 40–60 THB

items.name: Tam Kratoey Sisaket (in-town branch)
items.blurb: A central-town som tam spot focused on som tam, larb and fish fried with fish sauce, nicely savory. It's a regular lunch stop for people working nearby: food comes fast and it's comfortable to sit, good for a quick meal when you still want bold flavor.
items.price: Som tam 40–60 THB · fried fish 80–150 THB

items.name: Lert Isan
items.blurb: An in-town Isan spot with larb, koi, yam and a range of grilled dishes, good for coming as a group and sharing. The flavors are middle-of-the-road and you can adjust the spice to order. It's an easy place to sit for a while, good for dinner with drinks.

items.name: Saep I-Li Sisaket
items.blurb: An Isan spot on the main road into town that drivers like to stop at. The som tam and larb menu is complete, the flavors live up to the "saep" name, and there's jim jum and grilled dishes to order alongside. Parking is easy, so it's good for a stop mid-journey or a dinner without heading deep into town.
items.meta: On the main road into town, Mueang district

items.name: Saep Nua Station (Khukhan)
items.blurb: An Isan spot in Khukhan town for anyone heading to the south of the province. The menu of som tam, larb, koi and yam is varied and deeply savory, and it's a regular spot for Khukhan locals. Good to pair with a trip to the Khmer temples around there.

blocks.title: A straight word on koi
blocks.html: At many places in Isan, koi still comes raw or half-cooked. If you're not used to raw dishes, ordering cooked koi or cooked larb is safer, especially raw freshwater-fish koi, which carries a parasite risk. Just tell the shop you'd like it cooked, most are happy to do it.

blocks.text: Dishes to order at a Sisaket Isan place

items: Pla ra crab som tam — the southern-Isan headliner, savory from local fermented fish and seriously spicy. Tell the shop your spice level.
Larb & koi — pork or beef larb topped with fragrant toasted rice; for koi, order it cooked if you're not used to raw.
Grilled chicken & pork — eaten with sticky rice and jaew, the combo locals order constantly. At many places the grilled chicken sells out fast in the evening.
Tom saep & om — a hot, bold soup to cut the richness; om with offal or fish is a local specialty worth trying.
Fish fried with fish sauce / grilled fish — many Sisaket spots do freshwater fish well, and it pairs nicely with som tam.

blocks.text: Which areas are easiest for Isan food

blocks.html: In Sisaket town, som tam and larb shops are spread all over, especially around Nong Khrok, Mueang Tai, and the main road into town. If you're driving the Ubon route (Highway 226), there are roadside spots to stop at. And if you head to the south of the province around Khukhan and Kantharalak, there are regular local Isan places too.

items.name: In-town area (Nong Khrok–Mueang Tai)
items.blurb: Som tam, larb and grilled pork spots close together and easy to reach, good if you're staying in town.

items.name: Main road (Ubon route, Highway 226)
items.blurb: Roadside spots with parking, good for a stop while driving past or for dinner.

items.name: Southern area (Khukhan–Kantharalak)
items.blurb: Regular local Isan places, good to pair with a trip to the Khmer temples or the border.

blocks.title: If you're heading on to the border
blocks.html: If you plan to eat Isan food in the south and then continue to Pha Mo I Daeng or Khao Phra Wihan National Park, always check the border situation and whether the area is open before you go, since it can sometimes be closed or restricted. Have a backup plan ready.

blocks.text: Eating Sisaket Isan food the way locals do

items: Go to grilled-chicken spots before evening, since many sell out fast from around 5pm onward.
Carry cash. Most roadside som tam stalls don't take transfers or cards, though some have PromptPay.
State your spice level when you order. The standard here is noticeably spicier than central Thailand.
Order extra sticky rice, because som tam and grilled chicken only hit right with sticky rice.
If you're not used to raw dishes, skip raw koi and raw pla som, and go for cooked versions or cooked larb.

faq.q: Which Sisaket Isan restaurants do locals actually go to?
faq.a: The spots that come up most often in town include Som Tam Si Phao, Tam Kratoey Sisaket and Larb Sisaket. For seriously spicy larb there's Larb Saeng Siri, and if you want grilled chicken to take away there's Mae Noi Grilled Chicken around Kanthararom. They're all places locals return to again and again, at reasonable prices.

faq.q: Roughly how much do som tam, larb and koi cost in Sisaket?
faq.a: Som tam runs about 40–70 THB a plate, while larb and koi are around 50–120 THB depending on ingredients. Grilled chicken starts at about 60 THB a bird and up. Some old larb shops are cheaper than that, with plates at 30–40 THB.

faq.q: Is it safe to eat koi in Sisaket?
faq.a: Some koi is still served raw or half-cooked, especially raw freshwater-fish koi, which carries a parasite risk. If you're not used to raw dishes, order cooked koi or cooked larb instead. Just tell the shop you'd like it cooked, and most are happy to do it.

faq.q: What time should I go if I want grilled chicken?
faq.a: Go before the evening, since at many popular spots the grilled chicken sells out fast from around 5pm. To be safe, go in the afternoon up to about 4pm when there's more to choose from, or call ahead to reserve.

faq.q: Do Sisaket Isan places accept transfers?
faq.a: Most in-town and larger places have PromptPay, but some small roadside som tam stalls still take cash only. It's best to carry some cash just in case.
